title: AreaLight3D injects 2π too much energy into SDFGI with physical light units enabled
body: ### Tested versions - Reproducible in v4.7.stable.official [5b4e0cb0f] - The same code path is still present in master [00932449c] ### System information macOS 26.5.1 - Vulkan (Forward+) ### Issue description When physical light units are enabled, AreaLight3D works correctly with direct lighting, but becomes much brighter after SDFGI is enabled. The indirect light floods the scene and makes surfaces look washed out. The direct light packing path converts AreaLight3D luminous power to luminous intensity by dividing it by `2 * PI`: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/00932449c9f372b30301d8b5fdc1be70ec12b5c0/servers/rendering/renderer_rd/storage_rd/light_storage.cpp#L1032-L1044 ```cpp if (type == RSE::LIGHT_OMNI) { energy *= 1.0 / (Math::PI * 4.0); } else if (type == RSE::LIGHT_AREA) { energy *= 1.0 / (Math::PI * 2.0); } else { energy *= 1.0 / Math::PI; } ``` But both SDFGI light packing paths only handle omni and spot lights: - `SDFGI::pre_process_gi()`: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/00932449c9f372b30301d8b5fdc1be70ec12b5c0/servers/rendering/renderer_rd/environment/gi.cpp#L2000-L2012 - `SDFGI::render_static_lights()`: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/00932449c9f372b30301d8b5fdc1be70ec12b5c0/servers/rendering/renderer_rd/environment/gi.cpp#L2491-L2503 So the AreaLight3D intensity is written into SDFGI without the conversion and is exactly `2 * PI` higher than the direct lighting path. VoxelGI already has the expected AREA branch: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/00932449c9f372b30301d8b5fdc1be70ec12b5c0/servers/rendering/renderer_rd/environment/gi.cpp#L2998-L3007 This seems to have been missed when AreaLight3D support was added in #108219. Adding the following branch to both SDFGI paths fixes the problem: ```cpp } else if (lights[idx].type == RSE::LIGHT_AREA) { lights[idx].energy *= 1.0 / (Math::PI * 2.0); } ``` Additional note: the open HDDAGI PR #119869 inherits the same conversion block, so it appears to have the same issue. ### Steps to reproduce - Create a Forward+ project - Enable `rendering/lights_and_shadows/use_physical_light_units` - Add a closed room with diffuse materials - Add an AreaLight3D and set its intensity in lumens - Add a WorldEnvironment and enable SDFGI - Compare the scene with SDFGI enabled and disabled ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) [AreaLight3D-SDFGI-physical-units-MRP-v3.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31112281/AreaLight3D-SDFGI-physical-units-MRP-v3.zip)
